title: Headless CLI, MCP and JSON-lane guide

claims.text: The verb table documents tools, call, mcp, run, hook, snapshot, json, drain, serve, export, verify, operator ruling, doctor and mcp-config, each with its behavior, and the exit table fixes 0 for success, 2 for argument/schema/discovery refusal and 3 for domain, memory, concurrency, integrity, I/O or doctor failure.

Writes require a stable op_id: an exact retry replays the original result and commit prefix, reuse with changed content returns bad_op, and a stale expected_head returns stale_rev with nothing appended; replay lookup precedes the revision check.

Successful tool data is exactly {untrusted:DATA} and errors are {ok:false,code:CODE,detail?:DETAIL} to be used by code, while unknown costs stay null and Services.token_count remains None, so entries beyond 4000 bytes without a verified counter are refused with memory_debt.

decision.rule: Change here when headless verb behavior, exit codes, operation identity, or the headless guide example needs to change.
decision.failure: An agent assumes an absent tool exists, reuses an op_id with new content, or estimates token cost instead of cutting memory.

questions.q: Which headless verbs map to which exit codes on refusal?
